thread:
Rafael Mendes: quick on-call feedback request re: incident bot “recent deploys” context bundle. what should the default time window be?

Option A: last 2 deploys per service+region
Option B: last 60 minutes (could be >2 deploys)

Primary concern is noise in #incidents threads vs missing the relevant change. please vote w/ reactions below and any caveats.

Rafael Mendes: A = :one:
Rafael Mendes: B = :two:

Aisha Bello reacted with :two:
Miles Thornton reacted with :two:
Sean Gallagher reacted with :one:
Jacob Stein reacted with :two:
Connor O'Brien reacted with :one:
Devon Price reacted with :two:

Sean Gallagher: leaning A for default. in an actual incident thread, more than 2 deploy entries becomes scroll city. responders stop reading.

Aisha Bello: i voted B mostly bc last 2 deploys can miss the rollback/hotfix pattern if deploys are frequent. we’ve had “bad deploy -> rollback -> partial rollout” sequences where the *third* event was the important one.

Miles Thornton: +1 B. also multi-region: last 2 in us-east might be clean but you had 4 deploy attempts in eu-west during the same degradation window. time-based window makes correlation more intuitive.

Connor O'Brien: A isn’t as bad as it sounds if we include canary/hotfix metadata. last 2 deploys usually catches “what changed” for that service. window-based means if releases is flapping we’ll spam.

Jacob Stein: we can make it time-based but cap the number we print. e.g. “last 60m, showing most recent 2, +3 more (expand w/ command)”.

Devon Price: +1 to cap. can we also dedupe retries? release pipeline sometimes emits multiple events for the same version (retry, region retry) and it’ll look like “a ton of changes” when it’s just the same SHA.

Logan Wright: from observability side, time window aligns with “degradation started at ~T”. responders naturally ask “what happened in the last hour”. but please cap it.

Allison Grant: agree. if we do last 60m, we should clearly group by service+region and sort by timestamp. also annotate “manual rollback” vs “promote canary” so it’s not a wall of identical lines.

Sean Gallagher: ok cap solves a lot of it. but i still worry we’ll miss context when deploy cadence is low. if last 60m shows nothing, responders might wrongly assume “no changes”.

Miles Thornton: that’s solvable: if none in last 60m, we can include “last deploy was 3h ago (vX.Y.Z)” as a single line. basically “window + last-known” fallback.

Rafael Mendes: proposal based on thread:
- default window: last 60 minutes
- output cap: show up to 2 deploy events per service+region
- if >2 events in window: show “(+N more, use /incident-bot deploys --window 2h --limit 6)”
- if 0 in window: show last-known deploy line (timestamp + version) so it’s not misleading
- dedupe retries by (service, region, version, rollout_id) where possible

any objections?

Sean Gallagher: works for me. can we also make the default block collapsed/compact in Slack (one-liners) and avoid pasting full PR titles? just link.

Jacob Stein: yup, can do compact formatting. also will add an explicit “No deploy events in last 60m” line so it’s unambiguous.

Aisha Bello: +1. also can we log how often responders expand for “+N more”? would be a good signal if cap is too aggressive.

Rafael Mendes: good call — we’ll add a metric: deploy_collector.more_events_available + command usage.

Connor O'Brien: ok w/ this. i’ll help w/ dedupe logic / rollout_id mapping from release events.

Rafael Mendes: decision: default = 60m window w/ 2-event cap + “+N more” + last-known fallback. i’ll update ENG-2842 acceptance criteria + post in #eng-sre. thanks all.
